# 0. Introduction

```{r}
# R package **pcadapt** was developed to detect genetic markers involved in biological adaptation. 
# This package uses statistical tools for outlier detection based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA).
```

## 0.1. References

```{r}
# A tutorial for **pcadapt** is available on https://bcm-uga.github.io/pcadapt/articles/pcadapt.html
# Paper: Florian Privé, Keurcien Luu, Bjarni J Vilhjálmsson, Michael G B Blum, Performing Highly Efficient Genome Scans for Local Adaptation with R Package pcadapt Version 4, Molecular Biology and Evolution, Volume 37, Issue 7, July 2020, Pages 2153–2154, https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msaa053
```

# 1. Install and load libraries

```{r}
install.packages("pcadapt")
install.packages("qvalue")

library(qvalue)
library(pcadapt)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}

AND_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05 <- "/mnt/data2/Project_Polli_agro/Operational/4_data_analysis/01_snpcall/04_BCFtools/VCF_files_rm_assafora_kinship_GQ20_minDP8_genmiss_bialelic_polyonly/VCF_after_tidypopgen_filtering/AND_stk_rm_assafora_minDP8_GQ20_genmiss_bialelic_polyonly_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05.vcf.gz.vcf"

BOM_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05 <- "/mnt/data2/Project_Polli_agro/Operational/4_data_analysis/01_snpcall/04_BCFtools/VCF_files_rm_assafora_kinship_GQ20_minDP8_genmiss_bialelic_polyonly/VCF_after_tidypopgen_filtering/BOM_stk_rm_assafora_minDP8_GQ20_genmiss_bialelic_polyonly_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05.vcf.gz.vcf"

# We should use the `read.pcadapt` function to convert our .vcf files to the `bed` format
# `read.pcadapt` converts different types of files to the `bed` format and returns a character string containing the name of the converted file. 
# This file should be used as input for the **pcadapt** function.
# Supported formats: “**pcadapt**”, “**lfmm**”, “**vcf**”, “**bed**”, “**ped**”, “**pool**”.
# **pcadapt** files should have individuals in columns, SNPs in lines, and missing values should be encoded by a single character (e.g. 9) different from 0, 1 or 2.

AND_pcadapt_maf_0.20_fmiss_0.20 <- read.pcadapt(AND_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.20, type = "vcf")
AND_pcadapt_maf_0.15_fmiss_0.20 <- read.pcadapt(AND_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.15, type = "vcf")
AND_pcadapt_maf_0.10_fmiss_0.20 <- read.pcadapt(AND_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.10, type = "vcf")

LML_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20 <- read.pcadapt(LML_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05, type = "vcf")
```

# 3. Choosing the number `K` of Principal Components

```{r}
# The pcadapt function performs two successive tasks. First, PCA is performed on the centered and scaled genotype matrix.
# The second stage consists in computing test statistics and p-values based on the correlations between SNPs and the first K principal components (PCs). 
# To run the function pcadapt, the user should specify the output returned by the function `read.pcadapt` and the number K of principal components to compute.
# To choose `K`, principal component analysis should first be performed with a large enough number of principal components (e.g. K=20).

# Choosing `K`

## MAF = 0.20
AND_choosing_K_maf_0.20 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.20_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.20,
  ploidy = 2
)

## MAF = 0.15
AND_choosing_K_maf_0.15 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.15_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.15,
  ploidy = 2
)

## MAF = 0.10
AND_choosing_K_maf_0.10 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.10_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.10,
  ploidy = 2
)

## MAF = 0.05
AND_choosing_K_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)

BOM_choosing_K_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = BOM_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)

LML_choosing_K_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = LML_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 20,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)
```

# 4. Plot the best `K`

## 4.1. Screeplot

```{r}
## The ideal pattern in a scree plot is a steep curve followed by a bend and a straight line. 
# The eigenvalues that correspond to random variation lie on a straight line 
# The ones that correspond to population structure lie on a steep curve. 
# We recommend to keep PCs that correspond to eigenvalues to the left of the straight line (Cattell’s rule).

plot(AND_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "screeplot")

plot(BOM_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "screeplot")

plot(LML_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "screeplot")
# Based on the screeplot, K = 3 seems right.
# Same result with different MAF values
```

## 4.2. Score plot

```{r}
# Another option to choose the number of PCs is based on the ‘score plot’ that displays population structure. 
# The score plot displays the projections of the individuals onto the specified principal components. 
# Using the score plot, the choice of K can be limited to the values of K that correspond to a relevant level of population structure.

# Grouped by sampling sites
plot(AND_choosing_K_maf_0.20, option = "scores", pop = AND_pop_sampling_aligned)

plot(BOM_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = BOM_pop_sampling_aligned)

plot(LML_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = LML_pop_sampling_aligned)

# Grouped by landscape level 1 (SSF x LoA)
plot(AND_choosing_K_maf_0.20, option = "scores", pop = AND_popfile_landscape1_aligned)

plot(BOM_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = BOM_popfile_landscape1_aligned)

plot(LML_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = LML_popfile_landscape1_aligned)

# Grouped by landscape level 2 (SSF x Near_LoA x Far_LoA)
plot(AND_choosing_K_maf_0.20, option = "scores", pop = AND_popfile_landscape2_aligned)

plot(BOM_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = BOM_popfile_landscape2_aligned)

plot(LML_choosing_K_maf_0.05, option = "scores", pop = LML_popfile_landscape2_aligned)

# Different MAF values did not change the PCA pattern
```

# 5. Computing the test statistic based on PCA

```{r}
# For a given SNP, the test statistic is based on the z-scores obtained when regressing SNPs with the `K` principal components.

## MAF = 0.20, K = 1
AND_K1_maf_0.20 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.20_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.20,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K1_maf_0.20) 

## MAF = 0.20, K = 2
AND_K2_maf_0.20 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.20_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 2,
  min.maf = 0.20,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K2_maf_0.20)

## MAF = 0.20, K = 3
AND_K3_maf_0.20 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.20_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 3,
  min.maf = 0.20,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K3_maf_0.20)

## MAF = 0.15, K = 1
AND_K1_maf_0.15 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.15_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.15,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K1_maf_0.15)

## MAF = 0.15, K = 2
AND_K2_maf_0.15 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.15_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 2,
  min.maf = 0.15,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K2_maf_0.15)

## MAF = 0.15, K = 3
AND_K3_maf_0.15 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.15_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 3,
  min.maf = 0.15,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K3_maf_0.15)

## MAF = 0.10, K = 1
AND_K1_maf_0.10 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.10_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.10,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K1_maf_0.10)

## MAF = 0.10, K = 2
AND_K2_maf_0.10 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.10_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 2,
  min.maf = 0.10,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K2_maf_0.10)

## MAF = 0.10, K = 3
AND_K3_maf_0.10 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.10_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 3,
  min.maf = 0.10,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K3_maf_0.10)

## MAF = 0.05, K = 1
AND_K1_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(AND_K1_maf_0.05)

BOM_K1_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = BOM_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(BOM_K1_maf_0.05)

LML_K1_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = LML_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,
  K = 1,
  min.maf = 0.05,
  ploidy = 2
)

summary(LML_K1_maf_0.05)

## MAF = 0.05, K = 2
AND_K2_maf_0.05 <- pcadapt(
  input = AND_pcadapt_maf_0.05_fmiss_0.20,

summary(AND_K2_maf_0.05)

## MAF = 0.05, K = 3
```

# 9. Save outliers in .csv with CHR and POS info

## 9.1. Build VCF map

```{r}
make_vcf_map <- function(vcf_file) {
  vcf_lines <- readLines(vcf_file)
  vcf_records <- vcf_lines[!grepl("^#", vcf_lines)]
  vcf_records <- strsplit(vcf_records, "\t")

  data.frame(
    SNP_index = seq_along(vcf_records),
    CHR = vapply(vcf_records, `[`, character(1), 1),
    POS = as.numeric(vapply(vcf_records, `[`, character(1), 2)),
    ID  = vapply(vcf_records, `[`, character(1), 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 9.2. Create the VCF maps

```{r}

vcf_map_0.20 <- make_vcf_map(BOM_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.20)
vcf_map_0.15 <- make_vcf_map(BOM_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.15)

vcf_map_0.20 <- make_vcf_map(LML_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.20)

vcf_map_0.10 <- make_vcf_map(LML_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.10)
vcf_map_0.05 <- make_vcf_map(LML_vcf_fmiss_0.20_maf_0.05)
```

## 9.3. Function to extract Bonferroni outliers

```{r}
extract_bonferroni_outliers <- function(pcadapt_obj, vcf_map, alpha = 0.05) {
  
  results <- data.frame(
    SNP_index = seq_along(pcadapt_obj$pvalues),
    pvalue = pcadapt_obj$pvalues,
    maf = pcadapt_obj$maf,
    stat = pcadapt_obj$stat,
    chi2 = pcadapt_obj$chi2.stat
  )
  
  # remove loci with NA p-values (excluded internally by pcadapt)
  results <- results[!is.na(results$pvalue), ]
  
  # Bonferroni correction
  results$padj_bonferroni <- p.adjust(results$pvalue, method = "bonferroni")
  
  # join CHR, POS, ID from VCF
  results <- merge(results, vcf_map, by = "SNP_index", all.x = TRUE)
  
  # reorder columns
  results <- results[, c("SNP_index", "ID", "CHR", "POS", "pvalue", "padj_bonferroni", "maf", "stat", "chi2")]
  
  # keep only Bonferroni-significant outliers
  outliers <- results[results$padj_bonferroni < alpha, ]
  
  return(outliers)
}
```

## 9.4. Function to extract Benjamini-Hochberg outliers

```{r}
extract_BH_outliers <- function(pcadapt_obj, vcf_map, alpha = 0.05) {
  
  results <- data.frame(
    SNP_index = seq_along(pcadapt_obj$pvalues),
    pvalue = pcadapt_obj$pvalues,
    maf = pcadapt_obj$maf,
    stat = pcadapt_obj$stat,
    chi2 = pcadapt_obj$chi2.stat
  )
  
  # remove loci with NA p-values (excluded internally by pcadapt)
  results <- results[!is.na(results$pvalue), ]
  
  # Benjamini-Hochberg correction
  results$padj_BH <- p.adjust(results$pvalue, method = "BH")
  
  # join CHR, POS, ID from VCF
  results <- merge(results, vcf_map, by = "SNP_index", all.x = TRUE)
  
  # reorder columns
  results <- results[, c("SNP_index", "ID", "CHR", "POS", "pvalue", "padj_BH", "maf", "stat", "chi2")]
  
  # keep only BH-significant outliers
  outliers <- results[results$padj_BH < alpha, ]
  
  return(outliers)
}
```

## 9.5. Function to extract qvalue outliers

```{r}
extract_qvalue_outliers <- function(pcadapt_obj, vcf_map, alpha = 0.05) {
  
  results <- data.frame(
    SNP_index = seq_along(pcadapt_obj$pvalues),
    pvalue = pcadapt_obj$pvalues,
    maf = pcadapt_obj$maf,
    stat = pcadapt_obj$stat,
    chi2 = pcadapt_obj$chi2.stat
  )
  
  # remove loci with NA p-values
  results <- results[!is.na(results$pvalue), ]
  
  # compute q-values
  results$qvalue <- qvalue(results$pvalue)$qvalues
  
  # join CHR, POS, ID
  results <- merge(results, vcf_map, by = "SNP_index", all.x = TRUE)
  
  # reorder columns
  results <- results[, c("SNP_index", "ID", "CHR", "POS", "pvalue", "qvalue", "maf", "stat", "chi2")]
  
  # filter outliers
  outliers <- results[results$qvalue < alpha, ]
  
  return(outliers)
}
```

## 9.6. Extract and save the Bonferroni outlier tables

```{r}
# MAF 0.20, K = 1
AND_K1_maf_0.20_bonferroni_df <- extract_bonferroni_outliers(AND_K1_maf_0.20, vcf_map_0.20)
write.csv(AND_K1_maf_0.20_bonferroni_df, "AND_K1_maf_0.20_bonferroni_outliers_with_CHR_POS.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
